summary.headline: PCBL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 2,474 crores and PAT 20% to INR 74 crores, despite carbon black volumes of 134,180 tonnes.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 2,474 crores, EBITDA rose 12% to INR 310 crores and PAT grew 20% to INR 74 crores, on pricing discipline and cost actions. Carbon black volumes were weak as management let go of low-margin spot and Southeast Asian orders, and the company said it would not chase volume. Management kept the EBITDA-per-tonne guidance but flagged that the volume growth target of about 7% is now challenging. Crude moved back above $100 during the quarter, which lifted realisations, and Russian CBFS supply disruption is expected to keep feedstock tight.

financial_highlights.change: Exports down 18% QoQ per analyst question; no YoY figure stated

financial_highlights.value: About INR 19,800 (INR 17,500 excluding about INR 2,300 tariff refund)
186 million units, of which 108 million units sold externally at INR 5.34 per unit

segments.name: Carbon black (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Volume of 134,180 tonnes split into tyre grades 77,914 t, performance chemicals 39,698 t and specialty grades 16,568 t. Volume fell as spot business in Southeast Asia and domestic spot was let go on margin grounds.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 186 million units generated, 108 million units sold externally at INR 5.34/unit. Output was lower as Southeast Asia production was cut, and about 40% of power is used captively.

segments.name: Aquapharm
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 433 crores and EBITDA INR 42 crores on 24,253 MT. Home Care volume rose 7% YoY, Water Solutions and Oil & Gas each fell 20% YoY, and application-specific solutions grew 15%.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated double-digit growth in average EBITDA per tonne over FY26 levels.
Financial (EBITDA) guidance unchanged; volume growth of about 7% for FY27 described as challenging, so volume may come in below the initial plan.
Aquapharm targets double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and for H2 FY27, with new products (PBTC, GLDA, Green Chelates) as volume drivers.
Management expects a strong H2 but says the timing of recovery depends on market conditions; buying patterns expected to improve gradually.
INR 200-250 crore cost-saving programme (Project Alchemy) still targeted, with INR 10-15 crores captured so far; acceleration expected from coming quarters.
Coal distillation (backward integration) capex, part of INR 300 crore FY27 capex plan, is in final approval; announcement expected shortly.
Antidumping duty on HEDP and ATMP is provisional; not included in Aquapharm forecasts.
capex_capacity: Specialty carbon black capacity about 75 kt; Mundra Line 6 already commercialised and volumes can be dialled up as gas and feedstock become available.
Andhra capacity addition; total potential output of about 8 lakh tonnes including Andhra, about 2 lakh tonnes above current volumes, with a significant share intended for exports.
Super Conductive Black facility commissioned; Acetylene Black on track under the ECMS framework.
Nanovace (51% JV with Kinaltek) pilot at Palej producing samples now in internal qualification; silicon carbon composite development across Palej, Belgium and Australia.
US railcar infrastructure and Antwerp warehouse being set up to support export volumes.
Management said it may slightly postpone some capex decisions if needed.
demand_pricing: Crude moved back to about $110 (from about $70 at Q1 time), so there was no inventory give-back; only about INR 10-15 crores of Q1 inventory gain passed to customers early in Q2.
Price increase announced in the spot market, with further increases expected in November and December.
Russian refinery throughput at multi-decade lows, keeping global CBFS tight; Chinese coal tar prices firmed, supporting SE Asia prices.
Russian and Chinese imports into India declining over recent months as Russian supply tightened and Chinese coal tar costs rose.
Customers destocked in Q2; some tyre customers who stocked up in Q1 are expected to return volume in Q3.

Feedstock: about 80-85% previously sourced from the Gulf; US mix unchanged, with diversification to multiple US vendors and sourcing from Southeast Asia under negotiation, with a possible 1-2% premium on that volume.
Competition: some players are chasing volume at low prices in the domestic market, per management; management says this is unsustainable.
Europe market growth expected at about 1-2% next year; US tariff volatility still restraining large customers from shifting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How did inventory and pass-through of higher China coal tar prices play out in Q2, and what happens in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude stayed elevated rather than falling back, so there was no inventory give-back, with only about INR 10-15 crores of Q1 gains passed through early in Q2. Spot price increases are in place and further increases are expected in November and December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power revenue fall, and what drives power generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Aquapharm incurred about INR 10 crores of higher power purchase cost. Generation fell because Southeast Asia volumes were cut, and it should rise as production scales up this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cost reduction quantification and outlook under the INR 200-250 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the fixed cost decline was volume-driven, with about INR 10-15 crores from Project Alchemy so far. Management expects acceleration as initiatives are standardised over the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Export volume outlook for FY27 and the likely contribution from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a return to international growth as coal tar prices rise, with US railcar infrastructure unlocking volume. It expects significant export growth over the next few years through long-term tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance after a weak Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: The EBITDA guidance is unchanged, but the roughly 7% volume growth target is now challenging on raw material availability and competition. Volume may be lower than the initial plan, with spot opportunities in Q3 and Q4 to be pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Carbon black spread for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 19,800 per tonne EBITDA, of which about INR 2,300 was the US tariff refund, giving roughly INR 17,500 per tonne excluding the refund.

risks_watch: Crude price volatility (around $70 to $110 range in the period) affecting customer destocking and buying patterns.
Russian CBFS shortfall and Chinese coal tar price moves, which drive feedstock cost and spread.
Freight and war-risk premiums on feedstock and exports, with some export business unprofitable without pass-through freight.
Volume target risk: about 7% FY27 volume growth now seen as challenging.
Antidumping duty on HEDP and ATMP still provisional and unquantified.
Aquapharm H2 seasonality (Q3 dip) and US oil and gas investment hesitancy.
US tariff volatility holding back large export customers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and pricing discipline, but cautious on volumes: management repeatedly said it would not chase volume and that recovery timing depends on the market. It was less specific on quantifying cost savings and the timing of export and Aquapharm volume recovery.
key_quotes: Despite the volume headwind, we delivered and grew revenue by 14% to INR 2,474 crores , EBITDA grew 12% to INR 310 crores and profit after tax grew 20% to INR 74 crores, a testament to the improved pricing discipline and cost optimization effort.
And we are not chasing volumes. We would rather keep this capacity spare.
We reiterate our guidance of double-digit growth in average EBITDA per tonne over FY26 levels.

adds.what: Andhra carbon black capacity addition (total potential ~8 lakh t/yr incl. Andhra, ~2 lakh t above current volumes)
Coal distillation (backward integration) unit, part of INR 300 crore FY27 capex plan, in final approval

growth.why: Management held EBITDA-per-tonne growth (double-digit over FY26) and cost savings of INR 200 crores, but cut the ~7% FY27 carbon black volume growth target as 'challenging' after exiting low-margin spot orders; Aquapharm double-digit revenue growth held, backed by new products and a Mundra Line 6 and Andhra capacity narrative with no firm timelines.
